conclusion.ko: 볏과(Poaceae)를 지중해형 Testudo가 소화하지 못한다거나 일률적으로 급여 금지·제한해야 한다는 주장은 현재 확인한 근거로 지지되지 않는다. 야생 연구에서는 지역·계절에 따라 볏과가 회피되거나 적게 이용되는 개체군도 있지만, 다른 Testudo hermanni 및 Testudo graeca 자료에서는 실제 섭식이 확인된다. 따라서 Poaceae라는 과 수준 정보만으로 개별 식물의 급여 판정을 변경하지 않는다.
does_not_support: 지중해형 Testudo는 풀을 소화하지 못한다는 단정
야생 섭식 빈도를 사육 급여 비율로 변환
한 지역·한 종의 선택성을 Testudo 전체에 일반화

evidence.citation: Iftime A, Iftime O. 2012. Long term observations on the alimentation of wild Eastern Greek Tortoises Testudo graeca ibera in Dobrogea, Romania. Acta Herpetologica 7(1):105-110.
evidence.supports: Direct Ibera wild diet evidence; >95% plant matter and 25 plant species. Later species-account synthesis reports Poaceae genera including Dactylis, Dichantium, Festuca and Poa from this dataset.
evidence.limitations: Wild occurrence does not establish captive staple status, digestibility coefficient, safe percentage, or unlimited feeding.

evidence.citation: Del Vecchio S, Burke RL, Rugiero L, Capula M, Luiselli L. 2011. Seasonal changes in the diet of Testudo hermanni hermanni in central Italy. Herpetologica 67(3):236-249.
evidence.supports: The population consumed grasses in spring; Poaceae taxa reported include Avena barbata, Brachypodium sylvaticum and Catapodium rigidum.
evidence.limitations: Different Testudo species/subspecies and locality; presence in diet is not a captive feeding recommendation or digestibility trial.

evidence.citation: Meek R. Nutritional selection in Hermann's tortoise, Testudo hermanni, in Montenegro and Croatia.
evidence.supports: Poaceae were abundant in the study areas but rarely consumed, showing population-level selection away from grasses despite availability.
evidence.limitations: Does not demonstrate inability to digest Poaceae; the proposed easier energy assimilation of other plants is an interpretation, not a controlled grass digestibility experiment.

evidence.citation: Foraging ecology and vegetation characteristic of sites inhabited by wild populations of Testudo hermanni in Italy. SISVet proceedings, 2015.
evidence.supports: Poaceae genera Melica, Stipa and Vulpia occurred among selected/consumed families, while Poaceae as a family also showed a high negative selection index. This illustrates that occurrence and preference are not equivalent.
evidence.limitations: Conference proceedings/preliminary results; different species from Ibera; no controlled digestibility coefficient.

evidence.citation: Slimani T, El Hassani MS. 2006. Testudo graeca graeca feeding ecology in an arid and overgrazed zone in Morocco. Journal of Arid Environments 64(3):422-435.
evidence.supports: Strong selective feeding: five principal plant species made up 70% of identified material, with Fabaceae comprising 27%; abundant plants can be actively avoided.
evidence.limitations: Western T. graeca in an arid overgrazed locality; does not by itself establish a Poaceae digestion rule for T. g. ibera.

evidence.citation: Food choice of an Algerian population of the spur-thighed tortoise, Testudo graeca. African Journal of Herpetology 57(2):103-113.
evidence.supports: 4422 fragments from 44 tortoises included 13 dicot and three monocot species; dicots accounted for over 70% of diet fragments.
evidence.limitations: Monocot is broader than Poaceae and this study does not provide a controlled digestibility comparison.

evidence.citation: Leone C. 2021. Tortoise Diet (Testudo Species). Garden State Tortoise.
evidence.supports: Experienced Testudo husbandry source emphasizing a varied low-protein, high-fiber, calcium-rich diet.
evidence.limitations: Specialist husbandry source, not peer-reviewed primary evidence. Numerical nutrient targets must not be promoted to species-specific physiological thresholds without primary validation.

database_rule.rule: Poaceae family membership alone must not raise or lower a plant feeding verdict. Plant-level identity, toxicology, direct feeding evidence, part, maturity/form and taxon applicability remain separate evidence axes.
